newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGACOM CHIEF SAYS NO IPO PLANS FOR NOW.
newsitem.headline: BELGACOM CHIEF SAYS NO IPO PLANS FOR NOW.

text.p: Belgian telecommunications company Belgacom on Tuesday denied a newspaper report it was proposing a $2 billion-plus initial public offering for the state's 50.1 percent stake.
"For the time being, no initial public offering has been planned since this decision is up to the shareholders," chief executive officer John Goossens said in a statement.

The Wall Street Journal Europe earlier said that senior managers of Belgacom were urging the Belgian government to sell its controlling stake partly to help cover the company's huge unfunded pension liabilities.
The statement also quoted Goossens as saying the decision on any further privatisation was up to shareholders and not to Belgacom's management.
Belgian Telecommunications Minister Elio Di Rupo firmly opposes any further privatisation of Belgacom.
Goossens added it was management's concern however to remain competitive.
"In this respect, it is important...that company costs be decreased. A partial decrease in its contribution to the Pension Fund would help in this effort," the statement said.
The rest of Belgacom's capital -- 49.9 percent -- is owned by a consortium including Ameritech, Singapore Telecom, TeleDanmark and three Belgian investors.
